text:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO breach detected for /v1/generate (p99 > 3s) in us-west-2; automated mitigation attempted (route-fallback to trt8) and failed to recover to SLO. Pager: @alana :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: PAGER duty assigned to alana (oncall). Escalation level: page-1. Incident channel created.

alana: I'm on it. seeing p95 ~ 650ms, p99 spiking 3-8s for streaming endpoints. spikes correlate with high decode tail times.

ben: FYI we rolled trt9 + flashattn v2.1 to a subset of runtime nodes in us-west-2 ~ 12:10 UTC (5% canary). Canary looked fine during unit test, but production traffic shows intermittent tail stalls.

cheng: metrics: kernel compilecache miss rate jumped at 12:17, pagefaults per-second on gpu-hosts spiked. Host logs show repeated kernel OOMs then paging (~vmalloc fallback).

alana: can you paste the deploy details, ben? config/flags?

ben: deploy manifest snippet:
```
image: runtime:trt9-flashattn-v2.1
env:
  DECODE_FAST_PATH=true
  COMPILER_FLAGS=\"-O3 -march=native --enable-fast-kernel\"
resources:
  gpu: 1
  mem: 60Gi
```

ben: also enabled compiler flag `--inline-kv` in the JIT. we didn't see p99 locally.

diane: logs I grabbed from one of the affected nodes:
```
[12:19:12] decode: tail_latency=6874ms kernel:cu_launch_rc=-4 (EFAULT)
[12:19:12] paging: fallback to host memory, reclaiming kv-cache
[12:19:13] trace: compilepath: new-kernel v12 applied
[12:19:14] runtime: stream stall detected, connection reset
```

maria-cs: heads-up: two enterprise customers reported slow streaming responses and one raised a support ticket; they're on dedicated pools in us-west-2. They asked if this is a regression.

ops-sre: I'm seeing node-level memory pressure on g4dn-ish instances; major killer is large async JIT kernels allocating ephemeral buffers. Paging activity is causing long stalls when the GPU driver swaps pages.

alana: immediate mitigation options we can do now: 1) rollback canary to trt8 image (fast) 2) disable DECODE_FAST_PATH via config and restart on affected hosts (medium) 3) route traffic to unaffected region/ Dedicated pools (slower reconfig). Which do we want?

ben: Rollback is fastest. I can do a canary rollback and scale it to 100% if clean. Command: `rctl service set-image runtime us-west-2 runtime:trt8-flashattn-v1.9 --selector=canary`

cheng: hold — before 100% rollback, if this is paging+compile cache related we might still see churn as nodes purge compiled kernels. But rollback should stop any new nodes from getting v12 kernels.

diane: I propose step 1: scale canary down to 0% (undo the rollout) and mark affected hosts cordoned for deeper log capture. Step 2: enable traffic fallback to software decode on the critical customers (via route policy) while we confirm rollback.

alana: executing rollback now. executing: `rctl rollout undo runtime us-west-2 --to-image runtime:trt8-flashattn-v1.9 --timeout=300s`

alana: rollback started. I'll also cordon hosts with high pagefaults: `k8s cordon node/gpu-uw2-03` and `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets node/gpu-uw2-03`

pagerduty-bot: Acknowledged. alana has started a rollback. Estimated time to full rollback: ~6-8 minutes.

ben: rollback in progress. watching metrics.

(3m) ben: canary now at 0% — no new trt9 nodes coming up. existing trt9 nodes are being drained.

(6m) cheng: cordoned nodes draining. paging rate started to drop. p99 improved to ~1.2s but still above target.

maria-cs: letting customers know via support: \"We're rolling back a runtime kernel change that impacted streaming latency in us-west-2. We're prioritizing your traffic and will follow up after verification.\"

diane: note: even after rollback p99 isn't back to baseline. suspect kernel hot compiled artifacts still on disk / in GPU driver cache. we'll need to rebuild the kernel cache slower or restart driver to clear state.

ben: I can flush compiled kernel cache on affected nodes: `sudo /usr/local/bin/runtime-kernel-cache --flush` and restart runtime agent. Doing that on one node to measure impact.

(9m) ben: flushed kernel cache + restarted runtime agent on gpu-uw2-05. p99 dropped to 420ms on that node's shard. good sign.

alana: OK let's schedule a rolling cache flush on remaining affected nodes, 1 node every 30s to avoid capacity shock. cheng coordinate with SRE to avoid mass driver restarts.

cheng: agreed. starting rolling flush. Also patching compile config to disable `--inline-kv` until we root cause. I'll push a hotfix config: `COMPILER_FLAGS=\"-O3 -march=native\"`

diane: we should also create temporary routing rule to prefer dedicated pools for enterprise customers until we confirm stability. Maria, can you authorize priority routing?

maria-cs: authorized — applying priority routing now. message to customers: \"We've applied a mitigation and routed your traffic to dedicated capacity; latency should be restored within minutes.\"

(20m) alana: p99 back to 280-350ms cluster-wide, p95 ~ 90ms. paging activity normalized. Incident status: mitigated.

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged as mitigated. Assigning post-incident review owner: ben.

ben: initial root cause hypothesis: `trt9` runtime's new fused kernels + `--inline-kv` increased transient memory use and produced larger JIT artifacts that triggered driver-level paging on a specific GPU microcode variant in us-west-2; compilepath produced race in kernel evictions causing tail stalls.

diane: next steps for P-1: 1) run targeted repros with flashattn v2.1 + disabled inline-kv on staging GPUs of same hardware variant 2) collect full driver traces from affected hosts 3) roll forward small patch that disables inline-kv by default and adds an opt-in toggle for perf testing 4) update rollout playbook with kernel-cache flush step.

cheng: we should also add an automated health-check that monitors kernel cache miss rate and triggers a soft-fallback to trt8 if threshold exceeded for >2m. Filing infra ticket.

maria-cs: I'll prepare customer-facing note for impacted customers and coordinate an outbound once we have RCA.

alana: handing incident to ben/diane for postmortem and deeper RCA. I'm going back on rotation. Please keep me updated on major findings.

ben: taking over RCA + postmortem. timeline and artifacts will be in the incident board.

diane: creating followup incident PM: `INC-3745678901` with actions and owners.

ops-sre: logging kernel crash dumps to GCS: `gs://redwood-incident-dumps/3745678901/` — adding access for ben/cheng/diane.

alana: thanks everyone. Great rapid response. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status changed: RESOLVED (mitigated). Archive in 72h unless flagged for retention.
